headline: Failed House bill would have barred larger tax-exempt groups that took foreign money from giving to political committees for eight years.
what_it_does: The bill would have stopped certain tax-exempt organizations from giving money to political committees for eight years after they received a gift or contribution from a foreign national. It would have applied to 501(c) groups with at least $200,000 in yearly gross receipts or at least $500,000 in assets. A group that broke the rule would have owed a penalty equal to 200% of the political contribution. After a third such contribution, the group would have lost its tax-exempt status.

who_it_affects.group: Larger tax-exempt 501(c) organizations (such as charities, social welfare groups, unions, and trade associations) meeting the size limits
who_it_affects.how: They would have been barred from contributing to political committees for eight years after taking money from a foreign national, with penalties and possible loss of tax-exempt status for violations.

who_it_affects.group: Foreign nationals who donate to US nonprofits
who_it_affects.how: Their gifts would have triggered an eight-year ban on the receiving organization's contributions to political committees.
They could have lost contributions from tax-exempt groups that had received foreign money.
